Our Auld Enemy

"Never seen the face of defeat

Coming into the final stretch of the regular season, we find ourselves in an odd position. After a disastrous month or so, where the Sounders lost 9 out of 11 games, we went from shield contenders to playoff wannabees. Now we sit precariously above the red line with three points the only buffer between us and the prospect of no games in November. However, the MLS being what it is, if we dare to dream we see that despite our summer swoon, we are just six points off the supporter shield (granted: pretty much every other team has games in hand, but as 2013 showed us, games in hand aren't nearly as valuable as points in the bank).

As we look up to that top spot, who do we see but a familiar foe: our enemies to the north, Vancouver. Just this season, this will be our fourth of five matches against Vancouver in all competitions (One win, One Loss, One Draw so far). The familiarity with the Whitecaps goes well beyond this season and stretches back to the hollowed year of 1974, where on June 9th the Sounders beat the Whitecaps 2-0. Ever since then, the rivalry has been a hard fought battle on the pitch. While the scum to the south tend to arouse more vitriol, on the field the Whitecaps have been the harder fought rival. And wouldn't you know that as we face off with our opponents of old once more, the Cascadia Cup hangs in the balance! A single point or more is enough to bring the cup back home, but this game is more important than that. We need the points from this game to stay afloat in the playoff race, which is not a goal for us but an expectation. We need these points to keep moving up the standings and to allow us, however foolishly, to dream of keeping the shield.
